The square root of 2 is an irrational nu.why: One of the most often stated facts of mathematics, the textbook example of an irrational number, with a proof every course repeats. Thousands of exact mentions in Dolma across its spellings. It is provable, but a model meets it as a stated fact far more often than it could work it out.

notes: Stored edit (very_unlikely): stated thousands of times. Mathematics leaves out worlds: a fact about a number or a class of numbers rests on definitions and proofs, so no premise can give way and the edit leaves no consistent world to split between (README, Shape per topic). Derived queries ask what the edit forces through the definitions, holding the definitions fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. The four derived queries go through the definition of a rational number: a terminating or repeating decimal (chain through the class), a fraction whose square is 2, the commensurability of a square's diagonal with its side (the Pythagorean form of the same fact), and the length of its continued fraction (a role chain through the class: every rational number has a finite continued fraction). The conjunction with a side fact that used to be the fourth derived query is now the propositional 'and' query (2026-10-31). No background-belief query: the only other routes to these answers (the digits of √2, the incommensurability of the diagonal) state the same proposition in other words, so they cannot stay put while the edit holds. The near query (is pi irrational?) shares the relation and the topic and does not follow from the edit; its reference differs from the new answer (R6). Plausibility: a common belief of beginners, clearly false.
